questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'were'.

Key Points

  • Blank 4 is a part of conditional sentence.
  • [If ... were to + verb ..., ...]. 'Were to' is used in the present to emphasize that the conditional form is extremely unlikely or unthinkably horrible. Notice that this special form is only used in the if-clause.
  • Examples:
    • If she were to be rich, she would be horribly obnoxious.
      It is very unlikely that she would be rich.
    • If I were to have no friends, who would I spend my time with?
      Having no friends is a horrible thought.
    • If Nathan were to be my boss, this job would be intolerable.
      Nathan's being my boss is a horrible concept.
  • "Were to" is a special phrase usually ever preceded by words indicating you're making an assumption (like "if", "suppose", or "assume") to express a precondition. "If you were to offer me a job..."
  • "Would" describes the result of some action, and is already in the sentence. "I'd turn it down" is actually "I would turn it down".
  • Standing on the North or South pole is extremely unlikely, so 'were' should be used here.

Correct Answer: "At the height of its power, the Roman Empire..."

Additional Information

  • 'It’s' and 'its' are among the most commonly confused words.
  • They are pronounced the same, there’s a very small difference in how they’re written, and it’s also easy to mistake the contraction in 'it’s' for a possessive.
  • But the rules are very clear—'it’s' is the same type of contraction as “where’s” or “there’s,” and 'its' is a possessive just like “my” or “your.”
  • Correct Usage of 'it's': 
    • ​He doesn’t think its a good idea to spend all his money on video games.
    • He doesn’t think it’s a good idea to spend all his money on video games.
  • Correct Usage of 'it': 
    • Its been a year since the last time they met.
    • It’s been a year since the last time they met.
